hypothesis: Question: is the residual error of the current development leader (idea-e8e22d, flat_day_neigh, dev row RMSE 47.75, equal-date MAE 32.71) dominated by an inability of trees to extrapolate calendar level beyond the training range, and can an explicit 2011 seasonal profile plus a year-over-year growth term repair it? Prior evidence changed my view twice. (a) The recorded analysis 1d0f99d8 showed horizon-matched folds have huge negative bias (h1_last61 bias -53.4, h1_prev61 -50.3, weighted RMSE 85.2) while the actual development window had only bias -10.1 and RMSE 47.75, and development underprediction grew with date (first-half bias -3.69 vs second-half -16.37, daily pred/actual median 0.945). So the deficit is not random noise, it is a level/season extrapolation deficit whose size depends on how far the target period sits past the last trained calendar position. (b) The same analysis showed a constant level factor estimated from a 28-day internal tail was 0.9920 and made development RMSE 1.09% WORSE, so a scalar recency calibration is refuted as the fix. This proposal therefore tests a structured correction instead: a smoothed 2011 daily log-level profile S(doy) (+-10 day window) plus a robust median year-over-year offset g estimated from the 2012 training dates, applied either as a log-space offset on the target (genuine extrapolation) or as an extra feature (tree-mediated, expected to inherit the same extrapolation ceiling), with recent-90-day and all-2012 variants of g, plus base/anchor blends. Contrasting expected outcomes stated before execution: (i) anchor-offset branches win the horizon-matched internal folds by a large margin (fold bias moving from about -50 toward 0) AND transfer, giving development RMSE below 47.75; (ii) anchor wins the folds but overcorrects the milder May-June gap and development RMSE rises above 47.75 - this would be an informative negative result showing horizon-matched fold ranking does not transfer for level corrections, matching the failed 0.992 calibration, and the previously measured method would remain the best development reference; (iii) anchor loses on the folds and the program selects base_dayneigh, which should closely replicate 47.75 and act as a self-consistency check of the selection machinery. The anchor uses only training labels and the supplied evaluation calendar; day-aggregate and neighbour-hour features remain transductive over unlabeled evaluation covariates grouped by date, and this is reported in findings. Unverified until executed: all expected magnitudes above are authored expectations, not measurements.
